facts.raw_span: A 14-year-old Caucasian girl was transferred from a community emergency department after treatment for presumed anaphylaxis
immediately after ingestion she reported wheezing, cough, and swelling of the lips, face, and tongue
self-administered epinephrine (0.3 mg) at home
suspected food allergies (wheat, oats, tree nuts, chocolate, eggs, cow’s milk, and rice) without documented reactions
intermittent asthma
complex regional pain syndrome
delayed gastric emptying
major depressive disorder treated with fluoxetine, increased to 60 mg daily 5 months earlier
skin prick tests and serum-specific IgE to foods of concern were negative except for sensitization to several tree nuts without a supportive history of reaction with ingestion
testing for hereditary angioedema and baseline serum tryptase were normal
stridor, biphasic wheezing, and poor air movement without visible oropharyngeal swelling
afebrile, blood pressure 94/48 mmHg, heart rate 100 bpm, respiratory rate 30/min, and SpO₂ 100% on room air
